ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the diagram: In the diagram, capacitor C is connected between the upper and lower busbars on the right side; end a of potentiometer R is connected to the upper busbar, end b is connected to the lower busbar, and the sliding contact is also connected to the lower busbar through a wire. On the right side, L2 and R2 are also connected in series and then connected between the upper and lower busbars. Then reason: Since end b and the sliding contact are both connected to the lower busbar, the effective resistance actually connected by the potentiometer between the upper and lower busbars is that section of carbon-film resistance from end a to the contact. When the contact slides clockwise from the midpoint of the arc-shaped carbon film toward end b, viewed from the direction of the arc-shaped carbon film in the diagram, the length of the carbon film between a and the contact becomes longer, so the resistance connected into the circuit by the potentiometer increases. This resistance is in parallel with the right-side R2 and L2 branch; an increase in the resistance of the potentiometer branch will make the equivalent resistance of this part of the external load increase, and the voltage divided by the internal resistance of the power supply and the series branch decreases, so the voltage between the upper and lower busbars, that is, across the two ends of the capacitor, increases. From Q=CU and with C unchanged, the amount of charge carried by the capacitor increases.
